title.narrative: IUCN: Rights-based conservation for indigenous peoples

description.narrative:
Insatsen är ett projektstöd som kommer att stöda en effektiv design och genomförande av urfolkens rättigheter och miljö-rättsliga ansatser, skydd och hållbar naturresursförvaltning?? i land och territorier som tillhör urfolksbefolkningen i Central- och Sydamerika med Natur-baserade Lösningar baserade på urfolkssamhällenas egna visioner. Genom att stärka urfolkens strukturer och kapacitet att bidra till förvaltningen och deras territoriella integritet som bas för skydd av biologisk mångfald och ökad motståndskraft mot klimatförändringar ökar deras möjligheter att förbättra sin levnadsstandard.
Insatsen bidrar till att stödja urfolksgrupper i Latin-Amerika (Central-Amerika och Amazonas) genom att:
- urfolkssamhällen i eko-system med hög biologisk mångfald använder verktyg och metoder för att förhindra och minska hoten mot deras territoriella integritet,
- miljöförsvarare och deras ledare har förbättrat sin förvaltning, försvar och kommunikationskapacitet för en jämställd förvaltning och skydd av sina territoriella rättigheter,
- urfolkens organisationer och kommunikationsnätverk synliggör urfolkens och lokalsamhällenas bidrag till bevarande av naturen, förbättrat skydd och rapporterar hot mot deras integritet,
- miljöförsvarare och urfolkens organisationer samordnar sina agendor och åtgärdsförslag för att förhandla dem i internationella och regionala fora.

The initiative is a project support which ??seeks to support the effective design and implementation of the rights and environmental justice approach in processes of conservation and sustainable resource management on indigenous lands and territories in Central and South America with nature-based solutions from their own vision as indigenous communities. It will help to strengthen governance structures and capacities to contribute to the management and integrity of the territories as a basis for the conservation of biodiversity, the increase of resilience and opportunities to improve their livelihoods.
The project will support indigenous groups in Latin-America (Central America och the Amazon) by assisting:
- indigenous communities in highly biodiverse ecosystems to apply tools and mechanisms to prevent and reduce the treats to their territorial management.
- environmental defenders and leaders to improve their management, advocacy, and communication capacities for an equitable governance and defence of territorial rights.
- indigenous people’s organizations and communications networks to make visible IPCL contributions to conservation, strengthen the prevention and denounce threats to their integrity.
- environmental defenders and indigenous people’s organizations to harmonize their agendas ad action proposals to negotiate them in international and regional fora.

The project "Advancing towards effective conservation and territorial management with a rights-based approach: strengthening indigenous regional cooperation in Latin America" seeks to support the effective design and implementation of the rights and environmental justice approach in processes of conservation and sustainable resource management on indigenous lands and territories with principles based on nature-based solutions from the perspective of indigenous peoples; strengthen governance structures and capacities to contribute to the management and integrity of the territories as a basis for the conservation of biodiversity and the increase of resilience and opportunities to improve their livelihoods.
The project aspires to work on collaboration and dialogue actions between local actors (e.g. indigenous authorities and organizations) and with national and regional authorities and non state stakeholders, from an intercultural approach to consolidate governance structures, indigenous leadership and improve the inclussion and effective participation of women and youth in spaces for dialogue and decision-making on conservation and environmental issues.
Sida considers that the project aims to strengthen environmental governance, justice and a rights-based conservation approach within Latin America through empowerment and capacity building for organizations, IPLCs and environmental leaders in a sustainable, culturally adapted and inclusive manner, and in the full exercise of their rights to prevent and address threats to their territorial management.
In the long term the project will contribute to secure Indigenous peoples rights in conservation and territorial management of their territories and megadiverse ecosystems.

Period 2 (Jan 1/2024 Dec 31/2024)
The VOCES Project (voices, named after the focus of raising defenders and indigenous peoples voices with regards to environmental rights) has implemented a multi-scale intervention strategy that connects local actions with regional capacity-building and global advocacy. This integrated approach has been crucial for maintaining progress despite regional political challenges such as governance crises, institutional barriers, and climate-related disruptions. By remaining adaptable and fostering collaboration, this contribution continues to advance its mission of strengthening Indigenous territorial defense and promoting conservation through a rights-based approach.
Strengthening Territorial Management. In Peru, Ecuador, and Honduras, Indigenous communities living in highly biodiverse ecosystems are now using culturally appropriate tools and mechanisms to identify, monitor, and reduce threats to their territories. These toolsdeveloped in collaboration with local partners and Indigenous organizationsreflect a holistic approach that incorporates human rights, gender equity, and intergenerational knowledge. Key achievements include the creation of country-specific baselines, management plans, risk protocols, and community monitoring systems. Communication has played a central role in amplifying Indigenous voices: in Peru, digital tools and training have empowered local communicators; in Ecuador, environmental journalism has been promoted; and in Honduras, strategic communication planning has supported territorial councils.
Through the Small Grants Mechanism, 11 initiatives have been funded across the three countries, directly benefiting 817 people49% of whom are women. These initiatives have not only promoted biodiversity conservation and Indigenous rights but also fostered inclusive governance. Women have assumed leadership roles, contributing to community resilience and sustainability. Moreover, collaboration among 67 organizations has strengthened Indigenous leadership and expanded the contributions impact.
Building Leadership and Advocacy Skills. To support equitable governance and the defense of territorial rights, the contribution launched a regional intercultural training program for environmental leaders and defenders. Targeting at least 25 Indigenous leaders from seven countries, the program focuses on territorial management, rights-based conservation, and policy negotiation. It blends ancestral knowledge with Western methodologies and emphasizes the inclusion of women and youth.
A digital e-learning component will extend the programs reach to an additional 80 participants. To ensure long-term sustainability, a feasibility study is underway for the creation of an Intercultural online Training Center. The selection of a regional training partner selection was delayed, it has already been selected, with implementation scheduled to begin in June 2025.
Empowering Indigenous Communicators. The contribution is also working to strengthen Indigenous communication networks in Central America and the Amazon. These networks aim to raise awareness about conservation and threats to Indigenous communities. Training in journalism, multimedia production, and traditional story telling especially for women and youth has been a key focus.
Although the contribution faced delays in selecting a regional communication partner, it responded by revising its strategy and prioritizing local capacity-building. A new call for proposals was launched, and final submissions from pre-selected agencies are expected by the end of May 2025.
Expanding Civic Space and Legal Empowerment. To protect environmental defenders and promote inclusive civic spaces, the contribution has supported regional dialogue, legal empowerment, and collaboration. Activities included virtual consultations for the Regional Action Plan on Human Rights Defenders, application of the STAR conservation tool in Indigenous territories, and intercultural workshops that integrate Indigenous and scientific conservation knowledge.
The contribution also facilitated agreements to update regional maps and develop an Indigenous information system. In addition, it began documenting good legal practices under the Escazú Agreement, analyzing landmark cases to support environmental justice. Training manuals for judicial operators on climate change and human rights were developed to further strengthen legal frameworks and advocacy.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
